items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names and section-header comments are mostly clear, and code reads like `getOrderReturnedQtyMap`. But the UI code uses terse names: `const fb`, `const ta`, `inp`, `l`, `p`, `v`. Large template-literal HTML blocks are inlined with business-adjacent logic, which hurts scanning.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The new index.html is about 3128 lines, which caps this at accept. UI handlers do delegate to `window.shopTestAPI.*`. However, `updateAfterSalePreview` re-implements the refund formula (`round2((rawSum * order.payable) / order.subtotal)`, allReturned → remaining) separately from the API.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Quantities are validated (`Math.max(0, Math.floor(...))`) and import errors are reported without overwriting data. Remaining gaps: magic numbers such as the 0.9 member rate and coupon tiers, and the submit path uses `Number(inp.value)` without an integer check, leaving it to the API. All 25 hidden tests passed.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: There is a bill summary with discount rows and stacking rules, status badges, an after-sale preview with the refund formula, and toasts. A reset confirm modal exists, and paid-order cancel has a second confirmation. But `handleImportFromTextarea` overwrites data with no confirmation, and `submitAfterSaleModal` refunds immediately with no confirm.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls the same `shopTestAPI` functions (requestAfterSale, importData, getStats). Stats are derived each time. But money is float with `round2` rather than integer cents, and the after-sale preview duplicates the refund-allocation logic in the UI.
